proposals.before: Moreover, this boy will win fame and office early in life, yet his years will not exceed sixty or seventy."
proposals.after: Moreover, this boy will win fame and office early in life, yet his years will not exceed six times seven (forty-two)."

proposals.before: Moreover this boy will early attain name and rank, yet his years will not exceed sixty or seventy."
proposals.after: Moreover this boy will early attain name and rank, yet his years will not exceed six times seven (forty-two)."

proposals.before: He later died at forty-two, and the monk's words about sixty or seventy were thus fulfilled.
proposals.after: He later died at forty-two, and the monk's words about six times seven were thus fulfilled.
proposals.reason: The stated death age explicitly verifies 六七 as six times seven, so sixty or seventy is internally contradictory.

proposals.before: Later he died at forty-two; the words about sixty or seventy were thus fulfilled.
proposals.after: Later he died at forty-two; the words 'six times seven' were thus fulfilled.
proposals.reason: 六七 is multiplicative and its fulfillment is the stated age of forty-two.

proposals.before: Emperor Ming of Zhou praised him, summoned him, and appointed him Left Attendant Senior Master; he was promoted to Governor of Hanzhong and soon made Pillar of State, Third Rank.
proposals.after: Emperor Ming of Zhou praised him, summoned him, and appointed him Left Attendant Senior Master; he was promoted to Governor of Hanzhong and soon appointed an official with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies.
proposals.reason: 儀同三司 is Yitong Sansi, a ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, not the unrelated title Pillar of State; the repair restores the office named in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Emperor Ming of Zhou commended this, summoned him, and appointed him Left Attendant Senior Master; he was repeatedly promoted to Governor of Hanzhong and soon made Pillar of State, Third Rank.
proposals.after: Emperor Ming of Zhou commended this, summoned him, and appointed him Left Attendant Senior Master; he was repeatedly promoted to Governor of Hanzhong and soon made Yitong Sansi.
proposals.reason: 儀同三司 is Yitong Sansi and does not mean Pillar of State, Third Rank; the literal rendering should preserve the distinct office.

proposals.before: The authorities recorded his battle achievements and proposed to make him a Grand Pillar of State and grant him five thousand rolls of goods. Ban firmly declined: "Through the state's awesome authority I was able to settle my grievance; my heart was bent on private revenge, not on serving the state. The offices and rewards you would bestow I dare not accept."
proposals.after: The authorities recorded his battle achievements and proposed to make him a Pillar of State and grant him five thousand rolls of goods. Ban firmly declined: "Through the state's awesome authority I was able to settle my grievance; my heart was bent on private revenge, not on serving the state. The offices and rewards you would bestow I dare not accept."
proposals.reason: The Chinese has 柱國, Pillar of State; Grand Pillar of State would require 上柱國, so Grand overstates the proposed rank.

proposals.after: The authorities recorded his battle achievements and proposed to make him a Pillar of State and grant him five thousand rolls of goods. proposals.before: His younger brother Yi is treated in the "Literary Writings" biography.
proposals.after: His younger brother Kui is treated in the "Literary Writings" biography.
proposals.reason: The brother's name is 頍, read Kui (kuǐ), not Yi; this is a personal-name romanization error.

proposals.before: His younger brother Yi is treated in the "Literary Writings" biography.
proposals.after: His younger brother Kui is treated in the "Literary Writings" biography.
proposals.reason: The graph 頍 is read Kui (kuǐ) in the name 王頍, so Yi is an unsupported romanization.

proposals.before: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne he repeatedly rewarded him, promoted him to Pillar of State, Third Rank, and appointed him Governor of Pingyang.
proposals.after: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne he repeatedly rewarded him, promoted him to ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, and appointed him Governor of Pingyang.
proposals.reason: The source has 儀同三司, ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, not Pillar of State; the current translation conflates two separate ranks.

proposals.before: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne he repeatedly rewarded him, promoted him to Pillar of State, Third Rank, and appointed him Governor of Pingyang.
proposals.after: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne he repeatedly rewarded him, promoted him to Yitong Sansi, and appointed him Governor of Pingyang.
proposals.reason: The literal text should retain 儀同三司 as Yitong Sansi rather than replace it with the unrelated Pillar of State title.

proposals.before: The prefecture and county reported this to the court; the emperor sent Duke of Pingchang Yuwen Bi to visit their home and offer condolences and praise.
proposals.after: The prefecture and county reported this to the court; the emperor sent Duke of Pingchang Yuwen Bi to visit their home and commend them and inquire after their welfare.
proposals.reason: 勞問 here is an official visit of commendation and solicitous inquiry, not condolences for a death; the household is being honored for its harmony.

proposals.before: The prefecture and county reported this to the court; the emperor sent Duke of Pingchang Yuwen Bi to visit their home and offer condolences and praise.
proposals.after: The prefecture and county reported this to the court; the emperor sent Duke of Pingchang Yuwen Bi to visit their home and extend commendation and inquiries.
proposals.reason: No bereavement occurs in this passage; 勞問 means to visit, commend, and inquire after the household, so condolences is contextually incorrect.

proposals.before: His father Chun had been Administrator of Jiezhou during the Kaifu reign.
proposals.after: His father Chun had been Administrator of Jiezhou during the Kaihuang reign.
proposals.reason: The Chinese has 開皇中, the Kaihuang reign; "Kaifu" is a mistranscription of the reign name.

proposals.before: His father Chun had served as Administrator of Jiezhou in the Kaifu era.
proposals.after: His father Chun had served as Administrator of Jiezhou in the Kaihuang era.
proposals.reason: The Chinese has 開皇中, the Kaihuang era; "Kaifu" is a mistranscription of the reign name.

proposals.before: Nomarch Yang Da was inspecting Hebei; he came to the hut to offer condolences and renamed the village Filial Reverence Village and its lane Concord Lane.
proposals.after: Chief Counselor Yang Da was inspecting Hebei; he came to the hut to offer condolences and renamed the village Filial Reverence Village and its lane Concord Lane.
proposals.reason: 納言 is the central-government office of Chief Counselor, not a nomarch or regional governor.

proposals.before: Nomarch Yang Da was touring Hebei on inspection; he came to the hut to offer condolences, and therefore renamed the village where he lived Filial Reverence Village and its lane Concord Lane.
proposals.after: Chief Counselor Yang Da was touring Hebei on inspection; he came to the hut to offer condolences, and therefore renamed the village where he lived Filial Reverence Village and its lane Concord Lane.
proposals.reason: 納言 is the central-government office of Chief Counselor, not a nomarch or regional governor.

proposals.before: The great general commended this, and therefore enfeoffed Zigong with a posthumous office, appointing Denian as envoy to go to Lishi and conduct the ceremonial burial of Zigong.
proposals.after: The great general commended this, and therefore posthumously granted Zigong an office, appointing Denian as envoy to go to Lishi and conduct the ceremonial burial of Zigong.
proposals.reason: 贈官 means to grant an office posthumously; it does not mean to enfeoff someone.

proposals.before: The Lang cousins vied to die yet both lived; the Tian Yi couple died together yet won enduring fame; Derao's benevolence won over a host of bandits, Denian's loyalty moved the emperor who founded the dynasty — each story is praise enough.
proposals.after: The Lang brothers vied to die yet both lived; the Tian Yi couple died together yet won enduring fame; Derao's benevolence won over a host of bandits, Denian's righteousness moved the emperor who founded the dynasty — each story is praise enough.
proposals.reason: 昆弟 means brothers, not cousins; 義 is righteousness/duty rather than loyalty.

proposals.before: His younger brother Debei was clever and widely versed in the Five Classics, and between the Yellow River and north was acclaimed as a Confucian scholar.
proposals.after: His younger brother Debei was clever and widely versed in the Five Classics, and north of the Yellow River was acclaimed as a Confucian scholar.
proposals.reason: 河朔 means the region north of the Yellow River, not 'between the Yellow River and north'.

The same prophetic 六七 is fulfilled at age forty-two in s0110; sixty or seventy cannot be the intended sense in this multiplicative riddle.
終於四十二 proves that 六七之言 means six-times-seven, so reporting the monk's words as sixty or seventy contradicts the Chinese fulfillment.
